audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[] side/rating disagreed with content win[] on every one of 7 rows — full said Xerath L1-3, Skill L4-6/2items; content said Skill L1-3, Xerath L4-6, Sona 2items. Full-layer breakdown fields were generic template prose ('chord the contacts', 'aura economy') with no real ability names.
audit.why: Content's reasoning is grounded in real kit facts (Xerath's Arcanopulse has a long cast you can dodge early, his Eye of Destruction slow guarantees a follow-up from level 4-6, Rite of the Ancients snipes from off-screen at 6, and Sona's grouped Crescendo out-values his single-target snipe in teamfights) and matches Xerath's actual pattern; full-layer text was templated filler.
audit.corrected: Rewrote all 7 phases[].side/.rating to match content win[] (already correct on disk, no win[] edit needed), rewrote each why with the grounded reasoning, and rewrote breakdown.early/mid/cooldowns/trading/feeding/carry/late, ahead, tradeGood, tradeBad, enemyWin, and loading using real ability names (Arcanopulse, Eye of Destruction, Shocking Orb, Rite of the Ancients, Aria of Perseverance, Song of Celerity, Crescendo).

audit.why: Level 6 global-snipe ult threat, first-item poke peak (Ludens), and two-item Sona teamfight swing are now correctly reflected in the rewritten phases and breakdown.carry/late.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns already named Shocking Orb correctly but never distinguished it from the actual poke tools (Arcanopulse, Eye of Destruction) or the ult that decides most kills (Rite of the Ancients), so the field read as generic CC advice rather than matchup-specific sequencing.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now names all three relevant abilities and states exactly when to use Song of Celerity and Crescendo against this kit.
